steps.description: Create a Python script to perform the numerical experiment on neural network generalization as a probe for solution space rigidity. The script will vary constraint count (w) and measure the minimum hidden layer width (N_c) required to achieve zero violation on held-out constraints, determining if the solution space is rigid or fat.

plans.objective: [DIM: transport] The convergence of neural network weights during bootstrap training follows a Fokker-Planck equation in weight space, where the diffusion coefficient scales with constraint density $w$; thus $N_c(w)$ should exhibit sublinear scaling as increased constraint density suppresses weight fluctuations.

steps.description: Generate a Pareto front of neural network architectures by sweeping hidden layer widths (N_c) against constraint counts (w), train each configuration on bootstrap constraints, measure out-of-sample violation rates on held-out constraints, and determine the minimal N_c(w) achieving zero violations. This tests the hypothesis that constraint density suppresses weight fluctuations (sublinear scaling) vs. increases capacity requirements (superlinear scaling).
